name: resume.recruiter
description: Project Get a Job: the human half of the resume bar. Simulates a recruiter's first pass -- roughly the time it takes to read a headline, one summary line and the most recent role. Input is the resume text, then '=== JD ===', then the posting.

six_second_read.instructions: From the title line and first role alone, how confidently could a recruiter say what this person does and whether it matches the opening they are filling?
criteria: Cannot tell, or reads as the wrong function
Broad category is clear, the specific fit is not
Both the function and the fit to this opening are clear
Function, fit and a differentiating proof point are all clear

verification_risk.instructions: The resume contains at least one claim a recruiter could check against a public source -- a licence or certification registry, a public profile, a company record -- and find absent or contradicted.

profile_consistency.instructions: Nothing in the resume would contradict a standard public professional profile for the same person: same titles, same employers, same seniority, same dates.

obvious_next_question.instructions: What would a recruiter most likely probe first on a screening call?

criteria.scope_of_role: How big was the team, budget or remit really
criteria.recency_of_hands_on: How current and how hands-on the technical work is
criteria.why_leaving_or_gap: An employment gap, overlap or a move that needs explaining
criteria.self_employment: What the founder or consulting period actually was
criteria.specific_metric: Where a specific number came from

seniority_signal.instructions: What level does this resume read as, independent of the titles claimed?

criteria.above_posting: Reads senior to the posting, a flight-risk or comp-mismatch signal

narrative_coherence.instructions: The career reads as a deliberate progression toward this kind of role, rather than a set of unrelated moves.

reads_as_human.instructions: The writing reads as a person describing real work, rather than keyword-optimised or template-generated filler.

differentiation.instructions: How clearly does this resume say something a dozen other qualified applicants for the same posting could NOT say?
criteria: A clear differentiator supported by evidence
A specific, evidenced differentiator directly relevant to this posting

rules.reason: below 80% of the measured strong-control value (0.50)
below 80% of the measured strong-control value (0.72)
below 80% of the measured strong-control value (0.91)
below 80% of the measured strong-control value (0.73)

calibration.method: control-anchored, 2026-09-21, jev-1.13.0. STRONG = clean in-band senior resume; WEAK = generic no-content resume. Floor = 0.8 x STRONG, so a target can never exceed what a good document actually scores.

notes.boundary: A simulated first pass, not a real recruiter. No calibration against real screen outcomes exists. obvious_next_question is diagnostic, not pass/fail: it tells Mike what to prepare, and a clean resume can still return a question.
notes.disabled_questions: These questions could not separate a strong control from a deliberately weak one and their rules are removed until rewritten: none. Reporting a number from an unusable question would be a dashboard, not a gate.
notes.ceiling_warning: Six questions have a strong-control ceiling below 0.75, so a 0.90 target on them is unreachable by construction. Targets are now 0.8 x the measured strong control, per question.
